HM-Suiji
Aug 26, 2026

In Next.js, the previously experimental feature viewTransition has been disabled for some reason, and there is no mention of it on the official website. I believe this feature is very important, especially since the 16.3 documentation still includes content related to using viewTransition: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/view-transitions. However, it seems that the feature has been turned off, making viewTransition merely a decorative element. Will it be re-enabled in a future version? What was the reason for completely disabling it at this point?

icyJoseph

That flag used to gate the availability of ViewTransition when imported from react. That's not needed anymore, because ViewTransition went from React-experimental to React-canary.

  • Remove inert experimental.viewTransition flag #96098

Everything listed in the guide linked, https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/view-transitions, should work out of the box, without any configuration flags.

paramjeetn
Aug 30, 2026

In Next.js App Router, the experimental viewTransition configuration flag was paused/refactored because the underlying React core team introduced native first-class support for the View Transitions API in React 19 (<ViewTransition> / startTransition).

Current State & Recommended Approach:

Rather than relying on Next.js-specific experimental router flags, the modern standard is utilizing React 19's transition hooks or CSS native @view-transition rules:

'use client'
import { useTransition } from 'react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
export function NavigationLink({ href, children }: { href: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const router = useRouter()
  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition()
  const handleNavigate = () => {
    if (document.startViewTransition) {
      document.startViewTransition(() => {
        startTransition(() => {
          router.push(href)
        })
      })
    } else {
      router.push(href)
    }
  }
  return (
    <a onClick={handleNavigate} className="cursor-pointer">
      {children}
    </a>
  )
}

Once React 19 <ViewTransition> stabilization lands in general availability, Next.js App Router will integrate it natively at the layout boundary without experimental flags.
